comparator.name: Media and Information
comparator.academicYear: 2026–27 UvA curriculum and course catalogue, checked 2026-09-27
comparator.sourceNotes: The official 2026–27 course catalogue confirms a 180-EC, English-taught programme. Year 1 is a shared 60-EC media-studies foundation. From Year 2 the programme requires one of two 36-EC specialisations alongside 24 EC of digital methods and philosophy; the neutral official-order rule selects Cultural Information Studies, the first listed route, rather than optimising for UCR fit. Year 3 contains 42 EC of genuine free choice and an 18-EC research seminar and bachelor thesis. Zero-credit literacy, tutoring and writing requirements are excluded from the 180-EC component total.

routeSelection.basis: The programme requires a specialisation but the normalized target names neither route. Cultural Information Studies is selected because it is listed first in both the public curriculum and the 2026–27 course catalogue, independently of UCR course availability.

core: Media theory, history and critical analysis of contemporary digital culture
Digital information, platforms, archives and cultural institutions
Digital methods, coding, data analysis and empirical media research
Media-studies research practice, academic argument and independent inquiry
adjacent: Cultural information studies and digital humanities
New media, platform studies and digital cultural practices
Technology, society, identity and digital ethics
questions: How do digital media and information infrastructures shape culture and everyday life?
How can cultural data, archives and online platforms be studied critically and computationally?
How do media technologies transform communication, identity and public knowledge?

alternatives.label: Digital media, culture & information
alternatives.labelReason: The final curriculum balances media theory and cultural analysis with programming, data science, digital methods, communication, sociology and ethics.
alternatives.concept: A broad media-and-information pathway combining film and media analysis, communication and cultural interpretation with programming, data, digital methods, social research and critical study of technological change.
progression: Introductory programming, data science, media, mathematics and communication precede algorithms, artificial intelligence, advanced data work, media research, social theory and ethics. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and every course is placed in a verified 2026–29 offering; eight level-3 courses provide advanced depth.

alternatives.label: Cultural information & digital humanities
alternatives.labelReason: The completed programme joins coding and data analysis to archives, museums, literature, history, visual culture and independent humanities research.
alternatives.concept: Develops the selected Cultural Information Studies route through digital methods, coding and data alongside archives, museums, texts, images, cultural history and humanities research.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, eleven courses shift from communication, platform-oriented media, philosophy and advanced AI toward art history, museums, literature, cultural history and historical research. The resulting route uses computation primarily for cultural information and digital-humanities questions.
progression: Programming, data science, media and art-history foundations precede algorithms, AI, museum and heritage study, advanced data analysis, literary analysis and independent historical research. Formal prerequisites and verified semester offerings are respected, with seven level-3 courses.

alternatives.label: New media, platforms & digital society
alternatives.labelReason: The completed programme concentrates on media, rhetoric, audiences, organisations, platforms, identity, power and digital transformation.
alternatives.concept: Develops the New Media and Digital Culture direction as a social and communicative study of platforms, audiences, organisations, identity, power and technological change, supported by media analysis and empirical methods.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, ten courses remove advanced coding, AI and data analysis and add rhetoric, audience methods, organisational psychology, leadership, market research, digital transformation and politics. Compared with the digital-humanities route, fifteen courses differ, producing a clearly social and platform-centred pathway.
progression: Introductory programming, media, rhetoric, methods and sociology precede advanced film and media analysis, social theory, persuasive and creative communication, organisational leadership, market research and political analysis. All courses use verified offerings and formal prerequisites are met; eight are level 3.

selection.assessment: Three defensible, feasible and materially distinct UCR curricula are included: a balanced closest match plus the two official UvA specialisation directions. Further variants would recombine the same media, digital-methods and cultural-analysis evidence after the three-alternative maximum.

notes.text: UvA has more dedicated digital-media, platform, archival and digital-humanities coursework than UCR. The UCR alternatives combine relevant courses across media, communication, computing, data science, humanities and social science; they are coherent approximations rather than claims of course equivalence. The selected UvA route also retains 42 EC of genuine free choice, which is not used to invent fixed comparator content or improve apparent overlap.
